paras: The lynching of Matt Butts was the hanging of a Black man by a mob near Arlington, Early County, Georgia, on or about May 31, 1881. Butts had been accused of stabbing Maj. W. J. Bethea to death, and after his capture he was taken by a mob, reported as 200 men, and hanged to a tree. An Atlanta wire carried the news to papers in the Midwest and West, while a Georgia paper passed on a local account that called him Matt Horton.

According to an Atlanta dispatch of June 1, Butts, described as 'a negro', 'cruelly murdered' Maj. W. J. Bethea in Early County, stabbing him 'to the heart with the first thrust of the knife.' The Arlington Advance, as quoted by the Savannah Morning News, placed Bethea's killing in the week before its report. No report gives a motive or any account of the stabbing from the accused man's side.

The wire said the accused man was captured near Arlington and was then taken by 'a mob of two hundred men' and hanged, the Omaha Daily Bee adding that he was hung to a tree. In the Chicago and Wheeling copies, the capture or hanging took place 'yesterday', the day before the June 1 dispatch. The Arlington Advance gave a fuller local version: he was 'taken from the party who had him in charge by a party of armed men,' hanged to a tree, and his body riddled with bullets. Neither account says who had held him, where he was hanged beyond 'a tree', or at what hour.
No report of an inquest, arrests or any official response appears in the coverage.

The Atlanta wire ran on June 2 in the Wheeling Daily Intelligencer under the headline 'Summary Justice in Georgia', in the Chicago Daily Tribune as 'A Murder and Lynching', and in the Omaha Daily Bee's 'General News' column. Each copy stated the murder charge as fact and named the victim only as 'a negro' with no further description.

In Georgia, the Savannah Morning News ran the Arlington Advance item the same day among its 'Georgia Affairs' notes on fires, accidents and crops, without comment on the lynching. A week later a syndicated 'Tragical Tales' crime roundup repeated the wire in the Watertown Republican and the Mower County Transcript on June 8 and the Superior Times on June 11.

The wire named the man Matt Butts (printed 'Butta' in Wheeling), while the Arlington Advance called him Matt Horton. The roundup dated the capture 'on the 1st inst.', apparently the date of the dispatch rather than the 'yesterday' of the original wire.

reader.title: Lynching of Matt Butts
bases: A Black man accused of killing a white official was taken by a mob or armed party and hanged to a tree (A1, A3, A4).

The Atlanta wire says a mob of 200 men took and hanged the accused killer of Maj. W. J. Bethea, and the Arlington Advance (via Savannah) says armed men took him from his captors, hanged him and shot his body (A1, A2, A4); no lawful authority is mentioned and the stated reason was the alleged murder.
The Atlanta wire (A1, A2, A3) and the Arlington Advance as quoted in Savannah (A4) independently report the hanging of Bethea's accused killer, though they give different surnames.

accounts.label: Atlanta wire
accounts.gist: Matt Butts cruelly murdered Maj. W. J. Bethea with a knife; he was captured near Arlington and taken by a mob of 200 men and hanged (to a tree) the day before the June 1 dispatch.

accounts.label: Arlington Advance (quoted in Savannah)
accounts.gist: The negro Matt Horton, who murdered Major Bethea the week before, was taken from the party that had him in charge by armed men, hanged to a tree and his body riddled with bullets.

framing.detail: Northern and western dailies ran the Atlanta wire as a brief, the Wheeling paper under 'Summary Justice in Georgia', presenting the murder accusation as fact.
The Savannah Morning News passed on the Arlington Advance report in a column of state news items, stating that the man 'murdered Major Bethea' without comment on the lynching.

conflicts.note: The wire copies agree on Butts (Butta is likely an OCR or typesetting variant); the Arlington Advance, the local paper, gives Horton. Neither can be preferred from the texts.

conflicts.note: The two are compatible: the wire's 'captured ... and taken by a mob' can describe the same seizure from captors that the local paper states explicitly.

versions.value: Hanged 'yesterday', i.e. May 31, per Atlanta wire of June 1

conflicts.note: The June 1 wire dated the capture and hanging to the previous day; the later roundup's 'on the 1st inst.' appears to take the dispatch date as the event date.
